implement: legion-worker: the implementer's whole contract is here — the two code commits in the fixed order (implementation commit, push, gh pr create), the pre-push identity check, the skip-checks: true trailer rule for the handoff-only push, and the handoff file's shape.

legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the implementer writes the PR body from its template when the pull request opens and must put the paginated timeline read plus its filter-sensitivity control in its own E2E (implementer) line; it also fixes the six-string shape of each proof entry.
legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: the implementer runs the post-merge production check at the squash commit and may add no commit above the reviewer-approved head other than retro's.

legion-retro: the revived implementer runs retro — docs/solutions/<category>/<slug>-SMOKE-4.md naming, a retro with no learning commits none, and the last commit removes .legion/SMOKE-4/ from the head that merges, which acceptance criterion 3 depends on.
dispatch and dispatch-first: the production check's Dispatch message and the retro message go through the dispatch command, and Legion's issues never go to GitHub issues.
ce-simplify-code: named only to record that it does not run — the diff is one Markdown file, so the docs-only rule in pr-body.md gives no simplify pass and no Thermo line.
test: legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: defines what the tester verifies — re-drive the implementer's proof on the real surface rather than re-running CI, add the E2E (tester) line and the test handoff's own proof array, and record implementerProof {verdict, how}; a missing or blank implementer proof is a recorded failure, never a gap the tester fills.
legion-worker: the handoff write, the push order and the skip-checks: true trailer on the handoff-only push; it also states that CI's lanes are read, never re-run, as evidence.
dispatch and dispatch-first: anything the tester needs to say to a human goes through the dispatch command on SMOKE-4.
review: legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: fixes the reviewer's round order — read the code head's checks on GitHub, write and push the handoff, review the head that push made by SHA, then complete — and the approval's place in the merge gate.

legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the reviewer writes the body's 'Look at first' and 'Not proven / risk' lines, and 'none' is a finding while an unproven claim stands; it also says a docs-only diff runs no thermonuclear pair, so the absent Thermo line is not a finding.
legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: only if a thread exists — one disposition reply per thread, resolved individually by the implementer, never in bulk.
legion-worker: the review handoff's fields (verdict, counts, keyFindings), the push rule and the completion gate.

findings.finding: F1 — the spec's framing ('this run proves the follow-up fix: a daemon upgrade mid-flight never drops a merge that was already due') is not provable by this run, and no acceptance criterion mentions the upgrade. Migration 0045 queues at the upgrade rather than at every boot, no phase can restart the daemon, SMOKE-3's READY-to-merge window was ~2 s, and widening it needs a fail-on-demand.yml edit on the branch that acceptance criterion 3 forbids from reaching the merged head.
findings.answer: Plan §7 records this as the first spec departure and §6 D1 sends the choice to the architect: the plan builds a non-regression run of the final build (the daemon still merges a READY head itself, with no auto-merge armed), which is exactly what the three criteria state, and claims nothing about an upgrade in the bytes or the PR body. If the architect wants a real mid-flight proof, D1 names what it would need: an operator restart while the issue sits in awaiting_merge, the cluster-side 'outbox submitted a READY merge' log line, and a fourth acceptance criterion.

findings.finding: F2 — the spec never says whether smoke/SMOKE-4.md must assert anything about the upgrade-safe build; its content list names only the three SMOKE-3 facts, while the title frames the run as proving #1987's follow-up fix. The exact line-1 sentence must be decided before implementation, because it is written before the merge it describes.
findings.answer: Plan §1 pins both lines byte-for-byte and states why no build claim goes into them: no phase can read the cluster's image digest or the daemon log, and nothing GitHub serves separates #1987's submit path from the earlier one, so such a sentence would be permanently unfalsifiable on main. The build attestation stays on the Dispatch issue and in the PR body's Not proven / risk. §6 D2 gives the architect the override and says it must land before the implementer's first commit, and it names the cost of the default: main alone does not distinguish SMOKE-4 from SMOKE-3 beyond the key, date and PR number.

findings.finding: F3 — criterion 1's 'merged by Legion's daemon' is not observable on GitHub: the daemon's outbox row merges as the implement App, the same identity any other holder of that App's token would show. Only a cluster log line separated them for SMOKE-3, and it was posted by the operator, not a phase.
findings.answer: Plan §3 C1 splits the claim into four, proves merged_by login+id, the timeline's absence of auto_merge_enabled (durable) with its sensitivity control, the timestamped auto_merge reads (corroboration) and the repository setting (a neighbouring field, explicitly not a control), and records the remainder as the issue author's attestation in Not proven / risk. §6 D3 puts to the architect whether it wants the operator's log line; the plan does not make the run wait on it.

findings.finding: F4 — 'written by Legion's implementer App' does not say which object or fields are checked, and the naive reading fails: GitHub's squash sets web-flow as the merge commit's committer, and the branch's handoff commits are authored by the review App.
findings.answer: Plan §3 C1 item 2 fixes the objects and fields: author and committer login+id on the code commits (and retro's), .user on the pull request, author only on the squash commit with web-flow expected as its committer, and handoff commits authored by legion-reviewer[bot] explicitly not checked against the implement App. §2 resolves both App ids by reading users/<app>%5Bbot%5D rather than copying a literal from a previous run.

findings.finding: F5 — 'the date' names neither which date nor its format, and line 1 is committed before the merge it dates; this run starts at ~20:55Z, so the written date and the merge date can differ.
findings.answer: Plan §1 defines it as the UTC date on which the implementer commits line 1 (date -u +%F), YYYY-MM-DD, terminal in line 1 as in SMOKE-3, with a machine check any later phase can run without trusting the implementer: the commit's .commit.committer.date at <C1>, converted to UTC, equals it. A merge after 00:00Z on 2026-10-17 leaves the bytes standing; §5 records that as accepted, not a defect, and the PR body says so if it happens.

findings.finding: F6 — the spec fixes no wording or shape, yet 'exists on main' is only machine-checkable against pinned bytes, and the file must name a pull request number that does not exist when it is written; neighbouring numbers are live (#600, #601, #602 today).
findings.answer: Plan §1 pins the printf, the 259-byte line 1, the 2-line/299-byte file, the ASCII and trailing-newline assertions and line 2's regex, and requires every phase to rebuild the reference from the plan rather than from another phase's scratch file. It fixes the two-commit order (line 1, push, gh pr create, append line 2, push), forbids predicting the number, requires the pulls?state=all&head=sjawhar:legion/SMOKE-4 check, and makes the implement handoff name both <C1> and <H> so the one-line intermediate is not read as a defect.

findings.finding: F7 — criterion 3's allowed set ('the files Legion's retro step writes under docs/solutions/ for this run') is unknown when the plan is written and has no machine meaning without the naming rule, and the criterion does not say whether it is read on main's state or on the merge commit.
findings.answer: Plan §3 C3 writes it as a predicate over the squash commit's own immutable file list with the regex ^(smoke/SMOKE-4\.md|docs/solutions/[^/]+/.+-SMOKE-4\.md)$, says 0..n retro documents pass, adds the required rejection control (the same grep fed ci.yml, .fail-me and a .legion path prints all three), adds the .legion/SMOKE-4 404 at <M> with a 200 control at <A>, and adds a per-phase pre-push path guard. §1 states README.md and SMOKE.md are not touched.

findings.finding: F8 — 'exists on main' is point-in-time here: the same artefact class was deleted from main six minutes after SMOKE-2's production check by the operator's cleanup pull request, and fixtures are still landing hourly (#602 closed 20:55Z).
findings.answer: Plan §3 C1 pins every deciding read to <M>, the immutable squash commit, and makes the ?ref=main and compare/<M>...main reads timestamped observations rather than acceptance conditions (behind/diverged is a finding to report). §5 carries the risk and §6 D5(a) asks the architect to decide whether the operator is asked to merge nothing into the repository between this run's first push and its production check.

findings.finding: F9 — if any other actor merges the pull request before the daemon's row does, criterion 1 fails and the already-committed line 1 becomes false bytes on main; no rework recovers it.
findings.answer: Plan §5 lists it with today's evidence (sjawhar-agent[bot] opened and closed #600, #601 and #602), §3 C1 requires the matching Not proven / risk bullet in the PR body, and §6 D4 gives the architect the default: C1 fails, the phase reports, no phase edits the file or the spec to make the record true; abandoning and re-filing is the architect's call.

findings.finding: F10 — every criterion has a half no pre-merge phase can read; criterion 2 needs polling rather than one read; the head whose checks count is not the branch tip, since a skip-checks head returns zero check runs; and a pending gate at READY is expected under #1987.
findings.answer: Plan §3 splits each criterion into the implementer's pre-merge proof at <H>, the Not proven / risk bullet, and the production check at <M>; C2 requires reading at the newest non-handoff-only head with the compare ... all(startswith(".legion/")) gap proof, polling to completed both pre- and post-merge, and states that a queued gate at READY time is expected behaviour, not a defect, and that no phase quotes a pending verdict.

findings.finding: F11 — the repository's own SMOKE-3 learnings bind this plan in ways the spec does not mention, and SMOKE-3 itself failed one: the durable timeline read belongs in the first proof that makes the claim, a claim of absence needs a filter-sensitivity control, and a re-verification must rebuild the reference from the specification and re-run at a head the first phase never proved.
findings.answer: Plan §3 C1 puts the paginated timeline read and its select(.event=="committed") control in the implementer's own E2E line, §1 requires every phase to rebuild the reference from the plan's printf, and §4 Testing requires the tester to re-read at a head the implementer never proved and to record implementerProof {verdict, how}.

findings.finding: F12 — four spec statements the sources do not support as written: both sjawhar/legion#1987 and #1988 are open pull requests and the cluster's build is unreadable from any phase; #1987's migration is narrower than 'any pull request'; #1988 excludes the image-probe pod, so 'every Legion pod' overstates it; and SMOKE-3's own caveat about the merge path is inherited, not removed, by this run.
findings.answer: Plan §7 records the #1987-scope and #1988-scope departures with their evidence, §1 keeps all four out of the merged bytes, §6 D2 and D3 put the build attestation and the inherited caveat to the architect, and §3 C1 requires the inherited caveat in the PR body's Not proven / risk. The plan restates neither 'any pull request' nor 'every Legion pod'.

findings.finding: F13 — the acceptance evidence sjawhar/legion#1987 is waiting for lives in another repository, the spec names no such deliverable, and for SMOKE-3 the operator posted it rather than any phase.
findings.answer: Plan §4 'Out of scope for every phase' states that no SMOKE-4 phase writes to sjawhar/legion, so none attempts a cross-repository write, and §6 D5(b) sends to the architect the question of whether that comment is owed and by whom.

specDepartures.spec: The title 'Record a Legion run proving the upgrade-safe READY merge' and the sentence 'this run proves the follow-up fix: a daemon upgrade mid-flight never drops a merge that was already due.'
specDepartures.plan: Builds a non-regression run — the daemon carrying sjawhar/legion#1987's final build still merges a READY head itself, with auto-merge never armed — and asserts nothing about an upgrade in the merged bytes or the pull-request body. The upgrade question goes to the architect as decision D1.
specDepartures.evidence: sjawhar/legion#1987's migration 0045 queues once, inside the migration, for issues awaiting a merge at that moment, so an ordinary run on an already-migrated daemon exercises it as a no-op; no Legion phase can restart the daemon; SMOKE-3's READY-to-merge window was ~2 s (READY 19:23:17Z, mergedAt 19:23:19Z); and the published way to widen it edits .github/workflows/fail-on-demand.yml on the branch, which acceptance criterion 3 forbids from reaching the merged head.

summary: this run proves the follow-up fix: a daemon upgrade mid-flight never drops a merge that was already due
the issue title's claim that the run proves the upgrade-safe READY merge
outcome.scope: unchanged: the three acceptance criteria stand as written and the deliverable is still one file, smoke/SMOKE-4.md.

specDepartures.spec: sjawhar/legion#1987 'adds a database migration that queues the merge for any pull request that was already waiting for it when the daemon restarts onto a new build'.
specDepartures.plan: Where the plan restates it at all, it uses #1987's own scope: once, at the upgrade, for each issue awaiting its merge at its merger's READY head, still in the workflow, on an open pull request, in a tree that does not linger, with no queued row already; a restart that applies no migration queues nothing, and a by-hand READY gets none.
specDepartures.evidence: sjawhar/legion#1987's own pull-request body, read through the GitHub resolver during this plan's gap analysis.

summary: queues the merge for any pull request that was already waiting for it when the daemon restarts onto a new build
outcome.scope: unchanged: no acceptance criterion depends on this sentence.

specDepartures.spec: sjawhar/legion#1988 'protects every Legion pod from GKE Autopilot's balloon-pod eviction'.
specDepartures.plan: Makes no protection claim at all, and where one is restated, says 'issue and controller pods'.
specDepartures.evidence: sjawhar/legion#1988 annotates the two long-running pod kinds and deliberately excludes the image-probe pod; its own quality gate renamed the covering test to TestEveryIssueAndControllerPodIsProtectedFromAutoscalerEviction; the protection is bounded and is refused under a cloud.google.com/gke-spot selector. The phrase 'balloon-pod eviction' appears nowhere in #1988.

summary: sjawhar/legion#1988, which protects every Legion pod from GKE Autopilot's balloon-pod eviction
outcome.scope: unchanged: #1988 carries no acceptance criterion in this run.
